summary: Beiho Takashima (1875–1949) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Toyo University (circa 1896–1901), where he later held a post. He also founded Bukkyo Seito Doshikai.

Beiyin Deng works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Fudan University (BA), New York University (MA), and Arizona State University (PhD, 2016–2024), and was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of Missouri in 2024.

Bela Bhattacharya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She served as Professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and held a professorship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Beligalle Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Banaras Hindu University. He has served as a Professor at the University of Ruhuna and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Bemé Shyi Drol studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who completed his PhD at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein in 2001. By 2008, he served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

Benedetta Lomi is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned her PhD from SOAS. She held posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Virginia, and became Senior Lecturer at the University of Bristol in 2023.
Benhua Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Yang earned a doctoral degree from Nanjing University (2018–2021) and held a post at Anhui University.

Benigno Ferrario (1887–1956) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale." He served as Professor of Classical Languages and Philosophy at the University of the Republic from circa 1928 to 1956.

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Calcutta (MA) and University of London (D.Litt.). He taught at the University of Calcutta as Pali lecturer (1913–1914) and professor (1918–1948).

Benjamin A. Elman is a sinologist and historian who earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held major posts at UCLA (1986–2002) and Princeton University, where he directed the East Asian Studies Program.

Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., also studying with Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and Lopon Ugyen Rinpoche.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Stanford University (2003–2009) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. He was an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (circa 2009–2016).

Benjamin C. Ray is a religious studies scholar. He held the position of Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at the University of Virginia, where he was attested as faculty in 2000 and 2026.
Benjamin Fleming is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from McMaster University and held a post at the City University of New York (attested 2021).

Benjamin Fürchtegott Balthasar von Bergmann (1772–1856) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Jena before completing his PhD at the University of Tartu in 1816.
Benjamin Goldstein is a researcher in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.

Benjamin Guy Babington (1794–1866) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge (MD). He founded the Madras Literary Society, was honorary secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society, and served as physician at Guy's Hospital (circa 1840–1855).
Benjamin H. Rice (1814–1887) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Homerton College (1834–1836). In 1836, he served as a teacher and missionary for the London Missionary Society.
